Task Guide:

Simulate the thermal conductivity of a Lennard-Jones (LJ) system in LAMMPS. Define a simulation box with dimensions 10×10×20 in reduced LJ units. Set the number density of the fluid to 0.6 and the initial temperature to 1.35 in LJ units. Use a face-centered cubic (FCC) lattice to initialize atomic positions and assign a Lennard-Jones potential with a cutoff of 2.5σ. Create two temperature-controlled regions: a hot region at the bottom (z = 0 to 1) and a cold region at the top (z = 10 to 11). First, equilibrate the system using the NVT ensemble at 1.35 temperature for 1000 timesteps with a temperature damping factor of 0.5, then switch to the NVE ensemble while applying Langevin thermostats to the hot and cold regions to maintain temperatures at 1.70 and 1.0, respectively, using damping factor of 1.0 for both thermostats. Track the energy added and removed by the thermostats and compute the temperature difference between the regions. Run the simulation for 10,000 timesteps to establish a steady-state temperature gradient. Afterward, reset the Langevin energy accumulation and continue the simulation for an additional 20,000 timesteps while calculating the running average of the temperature difference. Divide the simulation box into bins along the z-direction and compute the temperature profile over time. Use the heat flux and steady-state temperature gradient to compute the thermal conductivity using Fourier’s law. As the final output, return the thermal conductivity in Lennard-Jones (LJ) reduced units. This is a large simulation, hence it is advisable to use multiple CPUs. Make sure all the associated files for this task (input files, log files, any other files) are in the /results/md_tutorials/13_July_2025/tool_calling/claude_35/comprehensive/task_7/task_7_trial_4 directory. # Initialization
units           lj
atom_style      atomic
dimension       3
boundary        p p p

# Create simulation box and atoms
lattice         fcc 0.93405  # Density 0.6 in LJ units
region          box block 0 10 0 10 0 20
create_box      1 box
create_atoms    1 box
mass            1 1.0

# Define potential
pair_style      lj/cut 2.5
pair_coeff      1 1 1.0 1.0

# Initialize velocities
velocity        all create 1.35 87287 dist gaussian

# Define regions for thermostats
region          hot block INF INF INF INF 0 1
region          cold block INF INF INF INF 10 11
group           hot dynamic all region hot
group           cold dynamic all region cold
group           mid subtract all hot cold

# Energy minimization
minimize        1.0e-4 1.0e-6 1000 10000

# First equilibration - NVT
fix             1 all nvt temp 1.35 1.35 0.5
thermo          100
run             1000
unfix           1

# Main run - NVE with thermostats
compute         ke_hot hot ke/atom
compute         ke_cold cold ke/atom
compute         temp_hot hot temp
compute         temp_cold cold temp
compute         temp_mid mid temp
compute         chunk all chunk/atom bin/1d z 0.0 20.0 40 units reduced
fix             temp_profile all ave/chunk 100 100 10000 chunk temp/atom file temp_profile.dat

# Apply Langevin thermostats to hot and cold regions
fix             hot_thermostat hot langevin 1.70 1.70 1.0 699483
fix             cold_thermostat cold langevin 1.0 1.0 1.0 584783
fix             2 all nve

# Run to establish steady state
thermo_style    custom step temp c_temp_hot c_temp_cold c_temp_mid f_hot_thermostat f_cold_thermostat
thermo          1000
run             10000

# Reset Langevin energy accumulation
fix             hot_thermostat hot langevin 1.70 1.70 1.0 699483
fix             cold_thermostat cold langevin 1.0 1.0 1.0 584783

# Production run
run             20000

# Print final statistics
variable        delta_T equal c_temp_hot-c_temp_cold
variable        heat_flux equal (f_hot_thermostat+(-f_cold_thermostat))/(2*10*10)
variable        conductivity equal ${heat_flux}/(${delta_T}/10)
print          "Thermal conductivity = ${conductivity}""}
